Numerical Schemes¶

This page describes the spatial and temporal discretisation used by LilyTorch. For the continuous equations see Mathematical Formulation.

On this page

    • Discrete differential operators

    • FFT solvers

Grid layout — staggered MAC grid¶

LilyTorch uses a Marker-and-Cell (MAC) staggered grid:

  • Pressure \(p\) — cell-centred.

  • Velocity \(u\) — \(x\)-face-centred (staggered \(+\tfrac{h}{2}\) in \(x\)).

  • Velocity \(v\) — \(y\)-face-centred (staggered \(+\tfrac{h}{2}\) in \(y\)).

  • Velocity \(w\) (3-D) — \(z\)-face-centred (staggered \(+\tfrac{h}{2}\) in \(z\)).

One ghost cell is added on every side of the domain, giving array shapes of (Nx+2, Ny+2) (2-D) or (Nx+2, Ny+2, Nz+2) (3-D). The interior is indexed as [1:-1, 1:-1, ...].

Ghost │  Interior cells (Nx)  │ Ghost
 [0]  │ [1] [2] … [Nx] │[Nx+1]

Discrete differential operators¶

All spatial operators are second-order central differences on the staggered grid:

Operator

Function

Stencil

Pressure gradient

operations.gradient(p)

Backward difference \((p_i - p_{i-1})/h\)

Velocity divergence

operations.divergence(u, v [, w])

Forward difference \((u_{i+1} - u_i)/h\)

Normal derivative

operations.normal_derivative(var, nx, ny [, nz])

\(\hat{n}\cdot\nabla\phi\)

Vorticity (2-D)

operations.vorticity(u, v)

Scalar \(\omega_z = \partial v/\partial x - \partial u/\partial y\)

Vorticity (3-D)

operations.vorticity_components(u, v, w)

\((\omega_x, \omega_y, \omega_z, |\boldsymbol\omega|)\), clipped [2:-2] to avoid ghost artefacts

Time integration — Heun’s method (RK2)¶

The full Navier–Stokes time-step follows a Heun predictor–corrector (explicit Runge–Kutta 2) scheme mirroring WaterLily.jl’s mom_step!:

Stage

Operations

Predictor

  1. Advection–diffusion on \(\mathbf{u}^n\) → \(\mathbf{u}^*\)

  2. BDIM meta-equation: \(\mathbf{u}^* \leftarrow \text{BDIM}(\mathbf{u}^*, \mathbf{u}^n_{\text{body}})\)

  3. Pressure projection with weight \(w = 1\) → \(\tilde{\mathbf{u}}\)

Corrector

  1. Advection–diffusion on \(\tilde{\mathbf{u}}\) → \(\mathbf{u}^{**}\)

  2. Rebase: \(\mathbf{u}^{**} \leftarrow \tfrac12(\mathbf{u}^{**} + \mathbf{u}^n)\)

  3. BDIM meta-equation

  4. Pressure projection with weight \(w = \tfrac12\) → \(\mathbf{u}^{n+1}\)

The advection–diffusion sub-step itself uses Forward Euler.

Advection (convection) schemes¶

The advection fluxes \(\nabla\cdot(\mathbf{u}\otimes\phi)\) are evaluated with one of six configurable schemes, selected by the convection_method YAML key:

Scheme

Order

Description

quick

3rd

Quadratic Upstream Interpolation for Convective Kinematics (Leonard 1979) with median limiter.

adbquickest

3rd TVD

Adaptive QUICK with Total Variation Diminishing (TVD) limiter.

cubista

2nd TVD

Convergent & Universally Bounded Interpolation Scheme for the Treatment of Advection (Alves et al. 2003).

van_leer

2nd TVD

Van Leer flux limiter (van Leer 1979).

cds

2nd

Central Difference Scheme — unbounded, for smooth problems.

semi_lagrangian

—

Stam (1999) unconditionally-stable backtracing. Useful for large time-steps but introduces numerical diffusion.

Smagorinsky LES — variable-coefficient diffusion¶

When the Smagorinsky subgrid-scale model is enabled (smagorinsky_cs > 0; see (5)), the constant-viscosity Laplacian \(\nu\,\nabla^{2}\phi\) is replaced by a variable-coefficient diffusion operator:

\[\nabla\cdot\bigl[(\nu + \nu_t)\,\nabla\phi\bigr]\]

On the staggered grid this is discretised as:

\[\sum_{d} \frac{ \nu^{\text{eff}}_{i+\frac{1}{2}}\, (\phi_{i+1} - \phi_i) - \nu^{\text{eff}}_{i-\frac{1}{2}}\, (\phi_i - \phi_{i-1}) }{(\Delta x_d)^{2}}\]

where the face-centred effective viscosity is the arithmetic average of the two adjacent cell-centred values:

\[\nu^{\text{eff}}_{i+\frac{1}{2}} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl( \nu^{\text{eff}}_i + \nu^{\text{eff}}_{i+1} \bigr), \qquad \nu^{\text{eff}} = \nu + \nu_t\]

The strain-rate magnitude \(|\bar{S}|\) is computed on the cell-centred grid using second-order central differences (torch.gradient). In 3-D this requires 9 velocity-gradient evaluations (one per \(\partial u_i/\partial x_j\) component):

\[|\bar{S}| = \sqrt{2\,S_{ij}\,S_{ij}} = \sqrt{ 2\left( S_{11}^2 + S_{22}^2 + S_{33}^2 + 2 S_{12}^2 + 2 S_{13}^2 + 2 S_{23}^2 \right) }\]

The eddy viscosity \(\nu_t\) is recomputed at the start of each advection–diffusion sub-step (i.e.once per Heun stage, or once per Euler step).

Computational cost. The Smagorinsky model adds a handful of element-wise GPU kernels per time step — negligible compared to the Poisson solve. Memory overhead is one extra scalar field (same size as pressure).

When smagorinsky_cs is 0 (the default), no strain-rate or eddy-viscosity computation is performed and the solver uses the original constant-coefficient Laplacian with zero overhead.

See the parameters page for configuration.

Poisson solvers¶

FFT solvers¶

Two FFT-based solvers are available, selected via poisson_bc_type:

Neumann (poisson_bc_type: neumann)

Spectral solve using the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT-II / IDCT-II). The eigenvalues of the discrete Neumann Laplacian are

\[\lambda_k = \frac{2}{h^2}\left(\cos\frac{\pi k}{N} - 1\right)\]

giving spectral accuracy. Only applicable when all boundaries are zero-normal-gradient (Neumann).

Free-space (poisson_bc_type: free)

Zero-padded convolution with a regularised Green’s function. The Green’s function is pre-computed (or loaded from poisson_folder cache) and stored in Fourier space. The RHS is zero-padded to twice the domain size, Fourier-transformed, multiplied by the Green’s function, and inverse-transformed.

See Mathematical Formulation for the Green’s function expressions.

Note

The FFT solvers are constant-coefficient: for a variable-density / \(\mu_0\)-weighted BDIM projection the coefficient is moved to the RHS as a division, which must stay bounded (the divisor uses the scalar fluid coefficient \(w\Delta t/\rho\), not the \(\mu_0\)-weighted coefficient that vanishes in the body band — see Multigrid vs FFT: why the RHS divisor must stay bounded). For genuinely variable-coefficient operators with strong contrast, prefer the multigrid solver below, which handles the variable coefficient directly.

Multigrid / MGCG solver¶

For variable-coefficient problems a geometric multigrid solver is used (class PoissonSolver).

V-cycle structure:

  1. Pre-smooth — nsmoothing sweeps of the chosen smoother.

  2. Restrict — full-weighting restriction of the residual and face coefficients to the next-coarser level.

  3. Recurse — repeat until the 2×2(×2) coarsest grid, where a direct solve is trivial.

  4. Prolongate — bilinear (2-D) / trilinear (3-D) interpolation to the finer level.

  5. Post-smooth — nsmoothing sweeps.

MGCG (poisson_method: mgcg) wraps the V-cycle as a preconditioner inside a Conjugate Gradient iteration.

Smoothers¶

Smoother

Key

Description

Weighted Jacobi

jacobi

\(p^{k+1} = (1-\omega)\,p^k + \omega\,\tilde{p}\), default \(\omega = 0.7\).

Red-Black Gauss-Seidel

rbgs

Lexicographic colouring; two half-sweeps per iteration. Better smoothing per sweep than Jacobi but less parallelisable.

torch.compile integration¶

LilyTorch can JIT-compile hot kernels via torch.compile with mode="reduce-overhead" (CUDA-graph fusion). Compilation targets:

Target

Config key

Advection–diffusion

compile_adv_diff

Force computation

compile_forces

SDF / \(\mu\) / normals

compile_sdf

Multigrid smoother

poisson_compile

Full V-cycle

poisson_compile

All compiled functions are module-level pure functions (not class methods), because torch.compile performs best on stateless functions. Variants are generated per (ndim, smoother) combination.

Note

Compilation incurs a one-time warm-up cost. For short simulations it may be faster to leave compilation disabled.
